# GNU

> The GNU Project promotes software freedom and operates a collaborative effort to develop free software since 1983, championing the four essential freedoms and copyleft principles.

GNU.org serves as the central hub for the GNU Project and Free Software Foundation, providing comprehensive resources on free software philosophy, endorsed GNU/Linux distributions, and a vast catalog of free software packages. The site documents the history and principles of the free software movement while offering practical guidance for education, contribution, and adoption of free software.

## Key Topics

- Free Software
- GNU Project
- Four Essential Freedoms
- Copyleft
- GNU/Linux
- Richard Stallman
- Free Software Foundation (FSF)
- Software Freedom
- GPL License
- Proprietary Software Critique
- Free Software Directory
- GNU Operating System
- User Freedom
- Open Source
- Free Software Philosophy

## Core GNU Philosophy & Overview

- [The GNU Operating System and the Free Software Movement](https://www.gnu.org): Homepage introducing GNU OS and free software movement since 1983
- [What is Free Software?](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/free-sw.html): Definition of free software covering four freedoms and copyleft
- [Philosophy of the GNU Project](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/philosophy.html): GNU Project philosophy covering four freedoms and copyleft principles
- [About the GNU Operating System](https://www.gnu.org/gnu/gnu.html): Overview of GNU OS history, Richard Stallman, and GNU/Linux
- [Proprietary Software](https://www.gnu.org/proprietary/proprietary.html): Analysis of proprietary software risks and nonfree software ethics

## Software & Distributions

- [Software](https://www.gnu.org/software/software.html): Directory of GNU software packages and operating system overview
- [GNU/Linux Distros](https://www.gnu.org/distros/distros.html): GNU/Linux distributions with FSF endorsement guidelines
- [List of Free GNU/Linux Distributions](https://www.gnu.org/distros/free-distros.html): Endorsed GNU/Linux distributions meeting Free System Guidelines

## Licenses & Legal

- [Licenses](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/licenses.html): GNU licenses including GPL, LGPL, and license compatibility information

## Documentation & Learning

- [Documentation of the GNU Project](https://www.gnu.org/doc/doc.html): Central documentation hub with manuals, FDL, and free software resources
- [Free Software and Education](https://www.gnu.org/education/education.html): Guide on free software benefits and classroom use in education
- [Recordings about GNU Philosophy and History](https://www.gnu.org/audio-video/philosophy-recordings.html): Richard Stallman and GNU philosophy video archive and recordings
- [Audio/Video](https://www.gnu.org/audio-video/audio-video.html): GNU philosophy and history recordings with free-format media library

## Contribution & Support

- [Helping the GNU Project and the Free Software Movement](https://www.gnu.org/help/help.html): Volunteer opportunities and ways to contribute to GNU development

## Optional

- [GNU's Who](https://www.gnu.org/people/people.html): Directory of GNU project contributors and maintainers
- [The GNU Art Gallery](https://www.gnu.org/graphics/graphics.html): GNU logos, artwork, and design contributions from community
- [Site map of www.gnu.org](https://www.gnu.org/server/sitemap.html): Navigation guide and directory structure of gnu.org website
- [Hyper Estraier @ www.gnu.org](https://www.gnu.org/cgi-bin/estseek.cgi): Full-text search interface for gnu.org using Hyper Estraier
- [Laugh along with GNU](https://www.gnu.org/fun/humor.html): Humor collection and jokes related to GNU and free software
